reviewNote: Drafted by Claude from the chart for faculty review. Not validated teaching content.
summary: 4 y with severe OSA for T&A, actively sick with a URI, drank juice 1 h 45 min before the case, and a family story that sounds like pseudocholinesterase deficiency.

asa.rationale: Severe pediatric OSA (oAHI 14, nadir 81%) with reactive airway disease and an active URI.

decision.rationale: Active URI within a week (Tmax 38.1 on 10/20, wet cough, purulent appearing rhinorrhea, coarse breath sounds, preop SpO2 95% and T 37.6) in a child with RAD and severe OSA having airway surgery carries high perioperative respiratory adverse event risk. Clear liquid at 0545 also violates a 2 h clear fast for a 0730 start. Discuss postponing about 2 to 4 weeks with the surgeon and family.

redFlags.evidence: Preop nursing note and 10/24 sick visit: wet cough, purulent appearing rhinorrhea, coarse breath sounds, fever 38.1 on 10/20; preop SpO2 95%, T 37.6.
redFlags.implication: Laryngospasm, bronchospasm, and desaturation risk are much higher with recent URI plus RAD, OSA, and airway surgery.
redFlags.action: Recommend postponing about 2 to 4 weeks; if proceeding, optimize (albuterol), avoid airway irritation, experienced provider.

redFlags.finding: Clear liquid 1 h 45 min before scheduled start
redFlags.evidence: Preop note: apple juice about 4 oz at 0545 in the car; case at 0730.
redFlags.implication: Does not meet a 2 h clear liquid fast.
redFlags.action: Delay start until 2 h after the juice at minimum.

redFlags.evidence: Mother's portal message 10/20 and preop note: maternal uncle ventilated for hours after appendectomy, could not break down a muscle relaxant.
redFlags.implication: Succinylcholine (and mivacurium) may cause prolonged paralysis; this matters for laryngospasm rescue.
redFlags.action: Avoid succinylcholine; plan laryngospasm rescue with CPAP, deepening with propofol, and rocuronium if needed; consider BChE activity and dibucaine number testing.

redFlags.evidence: PSG 09/14: oAHI 14, REM AHI 26, nadir 81%, peak EtCO2 54.
redFlags.implication: Increased opioid sensitivity and postoperative obstruction.
redFlags.action: Reduce opioid dosing, multimodal analgesia, awake extubation, overnight continuous pulse oximetry (ordered).

redFlags.evidence: Anesthesia history 04/2024: PAED 18 for 20 min, required propofol 1 mg/kg in PACU.
redFlags.action: Prophylaxis such as dexmedetomidine or propofol at the end, adequate analgesia, calm emergence with parent.

redFlags.implication: Aspiration or dislodgement during laryngoscopy and mouth gag placement.
redFlags.action: Document, discuss with parent, protect or plan removal.

redFlags.finding: Anesthesia consent not signed; separation anxiety
redFlags.implication: Consent from legal guardian required; anxious child.
redFlags.action: Obtain consent from mother; premedication (oral midazolam) or parental presence at induction.

planItems.item: Inhalation induction with sevoflurane, IV after induction
Oral RAE ETT per surgeon; avoid succinylcholine
Dexamethasone 0.5 mg/kg IV (8.5 mg) at induction per surgeon
Opioid sparing: reduced opioid dose, acetaminophen
Dexamethasone plus ondansetron (T&A is high PONV risk)
Awake extubation with OSA; emergence agitation prophylaxis
Overnight observation with continuous pulse oximetry

boothComplications.why: Reactive airway disease with active URI
